messages:
kai-devex: Quick heads-up — a user hit an import error in our JS onboarding sample after 4.3.2. They reported the worker bundler throwing: 

kai-devex: `Uncaught TypeError: The requested module "@redwood/sdk" does not provide an export named 'default'`

ana-eng: Do we still have the default shim in the ESM entry? We removed some CJS glue when tightening exports.

ana-eng: package.json exports currently: 

ana-eng: ```json
ana-eng: "exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs" }, "./package.json": "./package.json" }
ana-eng: ```

omar-runtime: That error means consumers using `import SDK from '@redwood/sdk'` will break because index.mjs only has named exports (no `export default`). Historically CJS allowed default imports via interop, but edge-only runtimes (Workers, Bun ESM loader) fail fast.

lex-qa: Also seeing TS errors in sample CI: 

lex-qa: `TS7016: Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood/sdk'.` Some bundlers/TS setups don't follow conditional "types" inside exports.

kai-devex: Short term: we should ship a patch that does 3 things: 1) add a default export shim in dist/index.mjs that re-exports the named createClient as default, 2) add top-level "types": "dist/index.d.ts" in package.json for TS resolution, 3) add explicit documented subpath exports for any public internal paths we expect samples to use (e.g. "./legacy").

omar-runtime: Agreed. I'll prepare the release PR with a minimal ESM default: `export { createClient as default } from './client.js'` so old imports keep working. We'll avoid reintroducing a wildcard export — prefer explicit subpaths for controlled compatibility.

lex-qa: I'll add smoke tests to sample-apps CI that run on Node+esbuild, Bun, and Cloudflare Workers to catch regressions earlier. Also add a tsc check against the published package to validate types resolution.

pkg-bot: npm-publish: Found no outstanding vulnerabilities; will run publish once PR approved.

ana-eng: Also add a short migration note in CHANGELOG: "If you relied on default imports or internal deep paths, update to named imports or pin older patch until 4.3.3 is available." Keep it brief.

kai-devex: Thanks — I'll send a quick message to support with the workaround (use `import { createClient }` or pin to 4.3.1) and link to the PR when ready.
